doc.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: New York, Blue Note and Jackie McLean
title: Vibes at the forefront of new music
summary: Reflection that vibraphone was not usually part of forceful new music and he was lucky to join.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: We’re going to stop. We’ve got to change the tape. Boy, Bobby, you got some stories, man.

. . . to have been there. I was playing an instrument where you didn’t really think of it as being integrated into a forceful type situation. You think of trumpet, saxophone, drums, bass, piano, but you don’t really think of vibes being at the forefront,
to start something new. That was – I was lucky that way, to be able to have joined in on that one.
You brought the right stuff at the right place at the right time, it seems.
